page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 architecture instance belonging to the E2 server family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.2 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. There is no bundled GPU or local NVMe storage included with this instance type, and it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a mixed profile. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core stress-ng performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and PassMark CPU scores fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached reads and writes is average. Conversely, single-threaded operations like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show poor performance, ranking in the bottom 10%, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak. Software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing benchmarks remain average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-highcpu-16 offers a resource-dense CPU configuration for workloads that do not require large memory footprints. The 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it a cost-effective option for compute-heavy tasks that are not memory-intensive. It is suitable for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, and lightweight LLM inference using small models, where CPU execution is prioritized over memory capacity or high-speed local storage.
